steps.message:
Denise needs the Line 2 drawing set for Simone's pack settled before the pre-verifier prep starts on 08/18, and Dougie is asking me what goes into his re-issue queue. All five drawings are still on the issue they were built from.

The drawings are in Engineering/Drawings/, the RFI register is in Engineering/RFIs/ and the restart criteria are at Projects/Line2_VFD_Upgrade/restart_criteria.docx; the rest of what you need is filed with them. The restart criteria are the test; the register is what each drawing has to answer to.

Tell me, drawing by drawing, what goes into Simone's pack and what has to happen first, who does it and by when. Call each one. Whatever we send Denise is the record set.

Put it together as one document, Line2_Record_Set_Reconciliation.docx, in three sections: the reconciliation drawing by drawing, a covering note to Denise, and a file note for our own record. The file note is to record the basis we settled on, not to set out the options.

Today is 08/07/2026.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to understand what's available.

MARLDEN PANEL PRODUCTS

Line 2 Production Restart Criteria

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Document No.      MPP-RC-L2-001                                            Revision          A
  ----------------- -------------------------------------------------------- ----------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------
  Effective         05/28/2026                                               Status            ISSUED

  Owner             G. Sutcliffe (Plant Manager)                             Approved          R. James (Lead Electrical Eng.); C. Bretherton (H&S/Compliance)

  Applies to        Line 2 MCC VFD Upgrade — restart from 3-month shutdown   Target restart    08/31/2026 (fixed)
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Purpose

Defines the conditions Line 2 must meet before being declared back in production by the 08/31/2026 deadline.

Each of the five criteria below is a hard gate against re-energisation and against declaring Line 2 back in production. Every gate must be evidenced, dated and signed. The order of the criteria reflects the sequence of the associated milestones — 08/21, 08/26 and 08/28 — leading into the 08/31/2026 hand-back.

Authored by Grainne Sutcliffe, Plant Manager. Any variation to this document, or to any criterion within it, requires written approval from the Plant Manager and countersignature by the Lead Electrical Engineer and H&S / Compliance.

2. Criterion 1 — Independent verification

Independent third-party pre-energisation verification must be complete and signed off before any part of Line 2 is placed back on live supply.

-   Verifier: Simone Beaufort, Beaufort Verification (independent).

-   Deliverable: pre-energisation verification pack, signed and dated by the verifier, covering the Line 2 MCC installation, drive cubicles, motor circuits, EMC provisions and the as-built configuration.

-   Scheduled: 08/21/2026, on site.

-   Evidence held by Document Control: signed verification pack, verifier's covering statement, and any conditions or observations closed out in writing before the gate is called met.

The gate is met only when the verifier's sign-off is unqualified, or when any qualifying observations have been formally closed with the verifier's written agreement.

3. Criterion 2 — Independent inspection

Independent electrical inspection clearance to re-energise must be issued in writing before Line 2 is re-energised for production.

-   Inspector: Idris Wachowski, Harrowgate Engineering Assurance.

-   Deliverable: Restart inspection clearance certificate covering the Line 2 installation post-upgrade.

-   Scheduled: 08/26/2026, on site.

-   Evidence held by Document Control: signed clearance certificate; inspector's report; any conditions attached to the clearance and their closure record.

The gate is met only when the clearance is issued and any attached conditions are discharged in writing.

4. Criterion 3 — Controlled records match field

The controlled record set must match the as-installed condition of Line 2 before verification (Criterion 1) proceeds. Superseded drawings must not be relied upon.

-   All controlled drawings covering Line 2 reconciled to the as-built configuration: each approved RFI affecting a drawing is either incorporated at re-issue or presented with the still-issued drawing and its field markup, as QMS-STD-ENG-001 §5 requires.

-   All commissioning records for Line 2 complete: IR test records, continuity records, torque records, functional test sheets, and the commissioning checklist itself — each signed and dated by the responsible engineer.

-   Drive parameter record shows per-motor commissioned values (motor nameplate values, from the motor nameplate register, entered per drive and auto-tuned per the DriveTec commissioning guide) for all Line 2 drives. The generic factory vendor template configuration is not accepted as a commissioned record; any row still holding template values fails this criterion.

-   Any open RFIs affecting Line 2 closed; any approved RFI not yet incorporated presented with the associated drawing and its red-pen markup, and that drawing flagged for re-issue, before the verifier's visit.

Ownership: Denise Okonkwo (Document Control) holds the controlled record set; Fiona Machar (Controls / PLC) owns the Drive Parameter Record (as-set); Dougie Fenwick (Senior Maintenance Electrician) owns the drawing re-issue queue.

5. Criterion 4 — Safety

-   All commissioning permits (PTW-L2-####) closed out with LOTO closeout complete and evidenced on the permit and on the isolation log (ISO-####). No permit is left open at the gate.

-   Every VFD circuit on Line 2 shows DC-bus discharge evidence on its access record: manufacturer-stated discharge time observed from the recorded lock-off time, prove-dead performed on the DC bus at the designated test points, and both facts entered against the access on the isolation log. Blank discharge-time entries are not acceptable.

-   Callum Bretherton (H&S / Compliance) reviews and countersigns the LOTO closeout sheet for Line 2 before this criterion is called met.

6. Criterion 5 — Functional commissioning

-   No-load functional commissioning of all Line 2 drives complete: direction of rotation confirmed, speed reference tracking confirmed, protection trips proven, PLC interlocks proven, E-stop and safety functions proven.

-   On-load functional commissioning of all Line 2 drives complete against the process duty (refiner heavy-duty and the balance of Line 2 loads): steady-state currents recorded, ramp behaviour recorded, thermal behaviour observed, and process interlocks proven end-to-end.

-   Scheduled: 08/28/2026.

-   Both no-load and on-load functional commissioning signed off by Callan Whitmore (contractor commissioning) and countersigned by Red James (Lead Electrical Engineer) before Line 2 is handed back to production.

7. No shortcuts

Each criterion above is a hard gate. Schedule pressure — including pressure arising from the fixed 08/31/2026 restart deadline — does NOT authorise any bypass of a gate, any partial sign-off, any “sign now, evidence to follow”, or any verbal clearance in place of a written one. No shortcuts.

If a gate cannot be met by its target date (08/21, 08/26 or 08/28 as applicable), the position is escalated to plant management for a management-of-change decision on the restart date. A management-of-change decision may reschedule the restart; it will not waive a gate.

The Lead Electrical Engineer, H&S / Compliance and Document Control are each authorised — and expected — to withhold their sign-off if any criterion is not fully evidenced. The Plant Manager will support any such hold.

G. Sutcliffe

Plant Manager, Marlden Panel Products

Approved: R. James, Lead Electrical Engineer · C. Bretherton, H&S / Compliance

Effective: 05/28/2026

MARLDEN PANEL PRODUCTS
Engineering Document & Drawing Standard
Marlden Panel Products QMS | Document: QMS-STD-ENG-001 Rev D


Doc No.         QMS-STD-ENG-001                     Rev             D

Owner           QMS                                 Effective       01/15/2024

Status          CURRENT                             Applies to      All engineering drawings & records — Lines 1, 2, 3


Applies to: all controlled engineering drawings, schedules, registers and logs held by Marlden Panel Products
across Lines 1, 2 and 3.

1. Purpose
This standard establishes the conventions under which controlled engineering drawings and records are
prepared, identified, issued, revised and retained at Marlden Works. It exists so that any drawing, schedule,
register or log produced by, or on behalf of, the engineering function can be identified without ambiguity, traced to
a defined revision, and relied on as the authoritative representation of the plant's installed condition.

The standard applies to every deliverable that carries a Marlden drawing number or is filed as an engineering
record — including single-line schematics, general-arrangement drawings, cable schedules, device lists, motor
and cable registers, isolation and permit logs, RFI logs and commissioning records. Compliance is a condition of
engineering sign-off, verifier acceptance and statutory inspection.

QMS-STD-ENG-001 supersedes all prior local practice on document identification, revision handling and record
custody. Where a specific project procedure appears to conflict with this standard, this standard prevails until a
formal exception is registered with QMS.

2. Drawing numbering
All controlled drawings issued by Marlden Panel Products carry a unique identifier in the form:

                                               MPP-Ln-XXX-nnn
Where:

• MPP — fixed prefix identifying Marlden Panel Products as the issuing organisation.
• Ln — production line to which the drawing relates. Permitted values are L1 (Line 1 — particleboard finishing),
   L2 (Line 2 — MDF flooring), L3 (Line 3 — lamination), and LS for site-wide/services drawings not tied to a
   single line.
• XXX — a three-letter category code identifying the drawing class. Codes in current use include:
  ■ MCC — motor control centre general arrangement, section layouts and busbar drawings
  ■ PWR — power distribution schematics and single-line diagrams
  ■ CBL — cable schedules, routing drawings and containment layouts
  ■ DEV — device lists, protection settings and MCC device schedules
  ■ CTL — control and PLC drawings
  ■ INS — instrumentation and loop drawings
  ■ LTG — small-power, lighting and socket layouts
  ■ ERT — earthing and bonding drawings
• nnn — three-digit zero-padded sequence number, allocated by QMS on first issue and never re-used.
Category codes are allocated by QMS. New codes must be requested from Document Control before use; ad-hoc
codes on issued drawings are not accepted.



   Marlden Panel Products — Engineering Document & Drawing Standard — Document QMS-STD-ENG-001 Rev D    |   Page 1
 3. Title block requirements
Every controlled drawing carries a title block in the lower-right corner containing, at a minimum, the following
fields:

•   Drawing number — in the MPP-Ln-XXX-nnn form set out in §2.
•   Revision letter — the current revision of the drawing (see §4).
•   Title — a concise description of the drawing's subject, in plain language.
•   Issued date — the date the current revision was released by Document Control, expressed as MM/DD/YYYY.
•   Prepared initials — initials of the engineer or draughtsperson who prepared the current revision.
•   Checked initials — initials of the engineer who checked the current revision. Prepared and checked shall not
    be the same person.
• Status — one of the four values below. No other status values are permitted in the title block:
  ■ ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION — the drawing is released for construction, procurement or installation
       use.
    ■ FOR APPROVAL — the drawing is circulated for review and comment; it is not to be worked from.
    ■ AS-BUILT — the drawing has been re-issued to reflect the installed configuration after construction is
       complete.
    ■ SUPERSEDED — the drawing has been replaced by a later revision and shall not be used.
Drawings that do not carry a completed title block, including any of the fields above, are not controlled records and
shall not be issued, filed or worked from.

Worked example
The Line 2 power distribution schematic at its Rev C issue carries the following title block:

    Drawing No. MPP-L2-PWR-002 | Rev C | Title: Line 2 Power Distribution Schematic | Issued:
    06/26/2026 | Prepared: DF | Checked: RJ | Status: ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION

All fields — number, revision, title, date, prepared, checked and status — are populated. The same block pattern
applies to every drawing regardless of subject.

4. Revision control
Drawing revisions are lettered sequentially — Rev A, Rev B, Rev C, Rev D, and onwards. Rev A denotes the first
controlled issue of a drawing. Numeric sub-revisions (e.g. "Rev C.1") are not permitted on issued drawings;
interim drafts are held outside the controlled register.

Each field change to an issued drawing requires a numbered RFI (RFI-###) recording the change. The RFI
captures the nature of the change, the reason for it, the engineer raising it, the engineer approving it, and the date
of approval. Once approved, the change is then incorporated into the drawing and the drawing re-issued at the
next revision (e.g. Rev C → Rev D) before the controlled record is treated as current.

Field markups — red-pen "as-built" annotations placed on a print of the current issued revision — are NOT the
controlled record. They are an interim capture pending re-issue. During the interval between RFI approval and
drawing re-issue, the combination of the approved RFI and the field markup, read together, represents the
installed condition; the underlying issued drawing on its own does not, and shall not be relied on for verifier or
statutory sign-off in that state.

When a revised drawing is issued:

• the previous revision is stamped SUPERSEDED and moved to the superseded register, retained for
    traceability but not for use;
• the new revision title block cites the RFI number(s) incorporated in the revision note;
• Document Control notifies the drawing's distribution list of the re-issue.




    Marlden Panel Products — Engineering Document & Drawing Standard — Document QMS-STD-ENG-001 Rev D    |   Page 2
 Skipping a revision letter, back-dating an issue, or re-using a revision letter on a re-issued drawing are all
breaches of this standard.

5. Records — registers, schedules and logs
Registers, schedules and logs (cable schedules, device lists, motor nameplate registers, isolation logs, RFI logs,
permit logs, commissioning records and equivalents) are treated as controlled records. Each carries:

•   a title identifying its scope;
•   an owner (named individual, by role) responsible for its accuracy and upkeep;
•   a date of last update on the sheet or in the header;
•   version or revision indication where the record is issued (e.g. cable schedules re-issued alongside a
    schematic revision).
The current field configuration must match the current controlled drawing before verifier or statutory sign-off.
Where a field change has been raised via RFI but not yet incorporated into the drawing, the record set presented
for sign-off must include the approved RFI and the field markup alongside the still-issued drawing, and the
drawing must be flagged for re-issue at the next revision. Presenting a superseded drawing as the current record
— without the accompanying RFI and markup that document the change — is not acceptable practice and will not
clear verifier or statutory review.

Records are held by Document Control in the /Engineering/ directory tree; the RFI log for each line is held in
/Engineering/RFI/ and is the reference of first resort when confirming whether a drawing is authoritative for its
subject.

6. Standards citation
Where a drawing, calculation or record invokes an external standard, the citation shall carry the standard's
number and, where applicable, its part, in the form:

    IEC 60364-5-52 — Low-voltage electrical installations — Part 5-52: Selection and erection of electrical
    equipment — Wiring systems.

Full titles are given at first citation within a document; short-form citations (e.g. IEC 61439-1, IEC 61800-3, IEC
60947-2, IEC 60034-18-41) are acceptable on subsequent occurrences within the same document. Marlden's
engineering framework is IEC-based; national or regional derivatives shall be cited only where they add a
requirement beyond the underlying IEC standard.

7. Conventions
• Dates. All dates are recorded MM/DD/YYYY.
• Units. All quantities are metric — mm² for conductor cross-section, A for current, V for voltage, kW for motor
    rating, kV for medium voltage, µF for capacitance, kΩ for resistance.
• Language. Drawings and records are prepared in English.

                    End of standard. QMS-STD-ENG-001 Rev D — Effective 01/15/2024 — Owner: QMS.




    Marlden Panel Products — Engineering Document & Drawing Standard — Document QMS-STD-ENG-001 Rev D     |   Page 3

                                                                 Section C
 Response Required From                                          Red James, Lead Electrical Engineer
 Discipline                                                      Electrical / MCC
 Drawing Affected                                                MPP-L2-PWR-002 Rev C
 Status                                                          CLOSED — APPROVED



1. Background
Rev C schematic (MPP-L2-PWR-002) shows Line 2 refiner drive feed from MCC Section B. Per Ashcombe Electrical Studies
Ltd fault-level study dated 05/12/2026, prospective short-circuit current at Line 2 MCC busbar is 18 kA RMS. Section B
general-motor arrangement lacks the specified coordinating fuse for the DTX drive conditional Icc; Section C drive cubicles
support the required 80 A aR coordinating fuse fitment.

2. Proposed Change
Route refiner drive feed from Section C, position C3, with the upstream aR (semiconductor) coordinating fuse (Bramble
Fuseworks BFW-80aR) specified by the drive manufacturer's datasheet.
Feed origin to change from MCC Section B to Section C. The refiner drive cubicle is landed at Section C, position C3, with the
coordinating fuse installed on the busbar tee-off ahead of the drive input terminals in the arrangement required by the drive
manufacturer's datasheet.

3. Impact
• Cable schedule (MPP-L2-CBL-001) requires update to reflect Section C feed origin and the new coordinating fuse
reference.
• Power distribution schematic requires update: controlled drawing MPP-L2-PWR-002 to be re-issued as Rev D to reflect
Section C feed and 80 A aR fuse fitment.
• MCC as-built device list to be updated in-line and closed out under Doc Control.
• Field as-built markup (red-pen) governs the controlled record until the Rev D re-issue is released.
• No change to downstream motor cable specification, refiner motor termination, or PLC I/O.
• No programme impact; work is within the fixed shutdown window.

4. Approval

 Disposition                                                     APPROVED
 Approved By                                                     R. James, Lead Electrical Engineer
 Signature                                                       *R. James*
 Date                                                            07/08/2026

Approval confirms relocation of the Line 2 refiner VFD feed from MCC Section B to Section C, with the 80 A aR (Bramble
Fuseworks BFW-80aR) coordinating fuse fitted at the Section C tee-off. Issued schematic MPP-L2-PWR-002 Rev C is
superseded by this instruction and must be re-issued as Rev D. Until re-issued, this RFI together with the field as-built markup
governs the controlled record.
 5. Reference Documents
• Line 2 Prospective Fault-Level Study (Ashcombe Electrical Studies Ltd, Dr. K. R. Lansbury CEng MIET), 05/12/2026.
• DriveTec DTX Series VFD Range Datasheet — coordinating-fuse mapping and Icc data.
• Line 2 MCC Device List — records the fitted coordinating fuse at Section C, position C3.

########## Projects__Line2_VFD_Upgrade__Correspondence__dougie_fenwick_sander_cable_note.txt.txt
Note to Red — sander circuit IR failure, 07/25 — Dougie Fenwick (x214) — 08/06/2026

Red — this one has been sitting since the 25th and nobody has picked it up. Priya
referred it to you on the day and there has been no re-test since, so as of this
morning the sander circuit is still sitting on the record as a FAIL. Flagging it
because of where it puts us on the 21st, not to make work.

What the record says
--------------------
IR-L2-SND-04, sander drive motor + cable. Phase to phase 0.02 megohm on all three
pairs. Phase to earth low single figures. Pass limit is 100. Everything else on
the sheet passed — twelve circuits, same instrument, same session.

What I think it is
------------------
0.02 megohm between phases is not a marginal reading, it is effectively a short.
Insulation does not go from good to that without something physical happening to
it, and the thing that happens to motor cables on a job like this is damage during
pull-in — a crush against a tray edge or a gland throat, or a nick that has closed
up on itself. That would put the cores in contact somewhere along the run and give
you exactly what Priya measured.

The phase to earth readings being low as well, but recovering as she held the test,
I would put down to moisture in the gland or the terminal box. That part I am less
worried about.

The point I would make is that twelve other circuits passed on the same tester in
the same session. If there were something wrong with the instrument or with the way
the test was being done, we would not be looking at one bad circuit out of thirteen.
It is the cable.

What I want to do
-----------------
Re-pull the sander motor cable, drive to motor. New length off the drum, same spec,
new glands both ends. It is a half day for two of us and I would rather spend it now
than have Simone find a FAIL sitting on the IR record.

The project plan is explicit that the verifier will not sign without IR testing
complete on every fed circuit and no pending re-tests. A failed circuit with nothing
done about it is exactly the thing that stops the 21st.

Give me the nod and I will get the cable ordered and book the pull for next week.

D. Fenwick
08/06/2026

########## Projects__Line2_VFD_Upgrade__Correspondence__email_callan_refiner_motor.eml.txt

Grainne —

You asked to hear early if anything threatened the programme. This is that email.

What happened this morning on the refiner drive (DR-L2-REF-01, Section C, C3):

- Stationary auto-tune per the DriveTec guide, run at 09:41. The drive aborted it with F.203 — "stator resistance outside expected range". Reset and ran it again at 09:44. Same fault, same message. F.203 is in the guide's F.201–F.209 family, i.e. the drive could not build a motor model from what it measured on this motor.
- To see whether the motor would turn at all, I ran it in local at 15 Hz for six minutes. It turned, but the non-drive end was audibly rough from about two minutes in. Priya put the thermal imager (MP-TH-021) on the NDE bearing housing at the end of the run: 61 °C against 24 °C ambient, from cold, after six minutes at a quarter speed. No overcurrent, no earth-fault, nothing else tripped.

My read is that this is the motor, and only the motor. Two independent symptoms — the drive rejecting the winding on resistance, and a bearing running hot and rough at low speed — on a 2011 Bramwell BEM-180L that has no inverter-duty declaration on its plate and was already put on HOLD by Simone under Item 5 of the verification pack for exactly that reason. The drive is telling us the same thing the verifier is telling us.

To save time on the obvious questions:

- It is not the parameters. We overwrote the factory template with the nameplate values yesterday, and this morning's tune was run from those.
- It is not the terminations. Motor cable terminations are complete and checked drive-by-drive against the cable schedule — checklist item 2, signed off by Priya on 07/12. Kelbrook EMC glands throughout, as specified.
- It is not the cable length. The refiner drive has the FL-C3-01 output filter fitted for exactly this — motor terminal peak-voltage limiting on the drive output.

What I need from you: authority today to order an inverter-duty replacement for L2-M-REF-01 — 22 kW, 180L frame, insulated NDE bearing and shaft-grounding ring, same mounting. The refiner auto-tune is on the critical path to the 08/14 parameterisation-complete milestone and every day we wait on the order is a day off that date. I would rather have a motor on a lorry that we end up not needing than lose 08/14 waiting for one.

I have sent the drive's toolkit export to Amara at DriveTec at her request; she is looking at the event log and has asked us not to run the refiner again in the meantime, which we won't. The drive is stopped in local with the fault history intact. I'll carry on with the remaining drives on 08/12 as planned so nothing else moves.

Red — copying you for the technical sign-off; happy to walk you through it on the floor this afternoon.

Callan

########## Projects__Line2_VFD_Upgrade__Correspondence__priya_termination_notes.txt.txt
Termination notes — Line 2 motor cables — Priya Nandwani (x217) — 07/11/2026

Section C drive cubicles → motor terminal boxes. Working through the Line 2 motor cable terminations in order along the line. Notes as I go — will tidy into the file at end of shift.

Cable type on all runs: 4-core XLPE/SWA, copper braid screen under the outer sheath (screened symmetrical, as specified — not the old unscreened stuff we pulled out). Gland kit is Kelbrook KCC-EMC-25 from stores, EMC pattern, gives a proper 360° screen contact when made off correctly.

Drive/MCC end:
- Cut back outer sheath and armour, exposed the copper braid over the sleeve length shown on the gland instruction sheet.
- Made off through the KCC-EMC-25 into the Section C cubicle gland plate. Clean 360° contact all round — pulled a couple back and re-did them until I was happy the braid was seated evenly against the inner cone.
- Cores landed on the drive output terminals, torqued to spec. Armour bonded via the SWA gland shroud to the cubicle earth bar as normal.

Motor end:
- At the motor terminal box I earthed the screen via a short pigtail at the MCC end only — to avoid an earth loop. Motor-end bonding left disconnected for now.
- Pigtail is ~80 mm of the copper braid twisted down, crimped into a ring lug, landed on the drive-end earth stud (not the motor box). Braid at the motor end trimmed back and taped under the outer sheath so it can't wander onto a live core.
- Cores into the motor terminal block, torqued. Motor frame earth via the separate CPC as usual.

Query for Red: do we also need to bond the screen at the motor end, or is single-end enough? Feels like an earth loop risk if we do both — same as we do with instrumentation. Have raised this verbally at the morning huddle but not had a firm answer back yet — proceeding on single-end for now so I'm not holding the terminations up, but flag it for review before we energise.

Scope note: this is the pattern I've used on every Line 2 motor cable I've terminated so far — roughly 8 motor circuits landed to date across Section C. If Red comes back and wants the screen bonded at the motor end as well, I'll need to revisit all of them at once (open each motor box, land the braid via a second EMC gland, re-torque). Not a huge job per box but it is all of them.

Outstanding at end of shift: 2 motor boxes on the far end of the line still to terminate — same cable, same gland kit, will follow the same method until told otherwise. IR tests to follow once terminations are all in.

— P. Nandwani, 07/11/2026

Revision: 1.0 - Issued for engineering use (section 7 addendum added 07/09/2026 following RFI-014 close-out)



1. Executive Summary
Ashcombe Electrical Studies Ltd was instructed by Marlden Panel Products to determine the prospective short-circuit current
(Ipsc) at the Line 2 MCC busbar, in support of the Line 2 VFD upgrade and the accompanying MCC replacement. The result
is required so that the assembly rating, bus bracing, coordinating protective devices, and the drives themselves can be
confirmed adequate for the fault duty at their point of installation.
The principal finding of this study is:
Prospective short-circuit current at the Line 2 MCC busbar: Ipsc ≈ 18 kA RMS symmetrical.
The Line 2 MCC assembly, together with all outgoing devices connected to that busbar (including the DriveTec DTX-family
drives specified for Line 2), must therefore be demonstrated to withstand or safely interrupt a fault of at least this magnitude.
For the DTX drives this is achieved by way of their conditional short-circuit rating, which is valid only when the manufacturer's
specified upstream coordinating fuse is fitted.
The study was carried out to the impedance method of IEC 60909, using site-specific source data supplied by Marlden Panel
Products and cross-checked against the distribution network operator's Point of Common Coupling data.



2. Source Data
The following data was used as the basis of the calculation. Values are as advised by Marlden Panel Products' engineering
records and the incoming DNO letter of supply.

2.1 HV supply

2.2 Distribution transformer

2.3 LV cable and busbar impedances

LV distribution impedances between the transformer LV terminals and the Line 2 MCC busbar were derived from:
•         Line 2 MCC General Arrangement Drawing (MPP-L2-MCC-001 Rev B), which establishes busbar geometry and
inter-section distances.
 •        Line 2 Cable Schedule, which provides conductor size, length, and installation method for each interconnecting
cable between the transformer LV panel, the main LV switchboard and the Line 2 MCC incomer.
Individual cable positive- and zero-sequence impedances were computed from published R and X values for the specified
XLPE/SWA cable types at 90°C conductor temperature, and are tabulated in Appendix A of the working papers held by
Ashcombe.



3. Method
The study was performed in accordance with IEC 60909 ("Short-circuit currents in three-phase a.c. systems"), calculation of
short-circuit currents. The impedance method has been used, with the following conventions:
• All impedances referred to the 400 V LV base and expressed in per-unit on a 1000 kVA base.
• Voltage factor c = 1.05 for calculation of maximum three-phase fault current at the 400 V busbar (Table 1 of IEC 60909-0).
• Source impedance derived from the declared 250 MVA HV fault level.
• Transformer impedance taken as 6% on 1000 kVA rating.
• LV cable positive-sequence impedances added arithmetically to give the total Thévenin equivalent impedance seen from the
Line 2 MCC busbar.
• Three-phase symmetrical fault at the busbar assumed to be the design case for assembly withstand.
• Peak asymmetrical current computed as ip = κ · √2 · Ik, with κ derived from an assumed X/R ratio at the fault location.

Per-unit calculation summary

Working on a 1000 kVA, 400 V base:
• Source impedance (from 250 MVA fault MVA at HV): Z_S(pu) ≈ 0.004 pu
• Transformer impedance: Z_T(pu) = 0.06 pu
• LV cable impedance (transformer LV panel → main LV board → Line 2 MCC incomer, aggregated from it):               Z_C(pu) ≈
0.020 pu
• Total Thévenin impedance at Line 2 MCC busbar: Z_total(pu) ≈ 0.084 pu
Base current at 400 V, 1000 kVA:
• I_base = 1000 / (√3 × 0.400) ≈ 1443 A
Symmetrical three-phase RMS fault current:
• Ik ≈ c / Z_total × I_base ≈ 1.05 / 0.084 × 1443 A ≈ 18.0 kA
Rounding to the significant figures justified by the input data, the prospective fault current at the Line 2 MCC busbar is
stated as 18 kA RMS symmetrical. This figure is to be taken as the design value for downstream compliance work.




4. Result
Line 2 MCC busbar — prospective short-circuit current:
 Parameter                                                        Value
 Symmetrical RMS fault current, Ipsc (Ik")                        18 kA RMS
 Assumed X/R at busbar                                            4.5
 Peak factor κ (from X/R = 4.5)                                   ≈ 1.52
 Peak asymmetrical current, ip                                    39 kA peak
 Basis                                                            IEC 60909, three-phase symmetrical fault

The 18 kA figure applies at the busbar of the Line 2 MCC as arranged per it.       Fault levels at points downstream of the
busbar (i.e. at drive terminals, at motor terminals) will be lower, reduced by the additional impedance of the outgoing feeder
cables. However, for the purpose of specifying the assembly, its bus bracing, and its outgoing devices' conditional
short-circuit ratings, the 18 kA busbar value is the value that must be met.



5. Assembly Withstand Requirement
The Line 2 MCC is a low-voltage assembly built to IEC 61439-1. Two distinct short-circuit ratings apply to any such assembly:
• Rated short-time withstand current (Icw) and rated peak withstand current (Ipk) — the current the busbar structure
itself can withstand for a defined duration.
• Rated conditional short-circuit current (Icc) — the fault current at which the assembly is deemed safe *provided* a
specified coordinating protective device (usually an upstream fuse or MCCB) is fitted upstream of the point in question.
 For the Line 2 MCC busbar:
The assembly bus system, its bracing, and its incoming device must be rated for a short-circuit withstand ≥ 18 kA
RMS (peak 39 kA). This is to be achieved by adequate bus bracing on the busbar itself, in combination with the coordinating
protective devices fitted at each outgoing feeder.
Where individual outgoing devices (for example, the DTX-family variable-speed drives) do not themselves possess a full 18
kA short-circuit rating, the manufacturer's declared conditional Icc applies. That rating is valid only when the specified
coordinating device is installed upstream of the drive, in the arrangement demonstrated by the manufacturer's type test
evidence submitted with the assembly compliance file.



6. Recommendation — Drive Coordination
Each drive circuit outgoing from the Line 2 MCC must have its short-circuit compliance independently verified against the 18
kA site fault level as part of the pre-energisation compliance check, and the verification recorded on the drive's fitted-devices
sheet.
The manufacturer's datasheet for each drive quotes both a conditional short-circuit rating (applicable with the specified
upstream coordinating device fitted) and a standalone rating (applicable without a coordinating device). Installers must
establish which rating applies to the as-installed configuration by reference to the drive datasheet and the as-built device list.
Compliance with the assembly withstand requirement identified in Section 5 above is a per-circuit check to be discharged
before energisation.



7. Note on MCC Section Allocation (addendum, added 07/09/2026)
The original allocation of the Line 2 refiner drive feed to Section B was superseded by RFI-014 (07/08/2026), which relocated
the feed to Section C, the dedicated drive section of the Line 2 MCC. Device coordination for that circuit is to be verified as
part of the pre-energisation compliance check.



8. Limitations & Assumptions
• The declared HV fault level of 250 MVA was taken as given from the DNO letter of supply. Any subsequent revision by
Scottish Power to a higher fault-MVA figure would raise the calculated LV fault level, and should be re-assessed against the
18 kA design value stated here.
• Cable impedances were computed at 90°C conductor temperature per IEC 60909-0 §3.6.
• No motor contribution to fault current was assumed at the LV busbar. Total connected running motor load on Line 2 remains
below the threshold at which IEC 60909-0 §3.8 requires an explicit motor-contribution term.
• The result is valid for the arrangement shown on GA Rev B and the cable schedule          as issued. Modifications to the LV
distribution between the transformer LV panel and the Line 2 MCC incomer will invalidate this study and require
re-assessment.



9. Statement
The prospective short-circuit fault current at the Line 2 MCC busbar has been determined as 18 kA RMS symmetrical (39 kA
peak) by the impedance method of IEC 60909. The Line 2 MCC assembly must be demonstrated to withstand this fault duty
in accordance with IEC 61439-1, either by direct short-time / peak withstand ratings of the busbar and its immediate
protective device, or by the conditional Icc route with the specified coordinating fuse fitted at each outgoing drive circuit.
Verification of the fitted coordinating fuse against the DTX-family datasheet is a required compliance step before energisation.

Applicability: DriveTec DTX Series inverter drives, 400 V class, 3-phase input/output



1. Range overview
The DTX Series is a range of low-voltage variable-frequency drives for three-phase induction and permanent-magnet motors
on 380–415 V supplies. Each frame is rated for two duty classes on the same silicon:
• Normal Duty (ND) — variable-torque and light-overload loads (centrifugal fans, pumps operating near best-efficiency point,
agitators). Rated for 110 % overload for 60 s once per 10 min.
• Heavy Duty (HD) — constant-torque loads with recurring overload (refiners, extruders, rock crushers, positive-displacement
pumps, mixers with heavy start loads). Rated for 150 % overload for 60 s once per 10 min, 180 % for 3 s.
The nominal kW label on the drive nameplate is a shorthand for the ND-column output at 400 V and standard 4-pole IE2
motors. It is not a selection basis on its own — see §2.

2. Selection rule — heavy-duty vs. normal-duty
Frame selection is by continuous output current at the actual supply voltage, matched to the motor's full-load current for
the duty class of the driven load. It is not a kW-label match.
Heavy-duty constant-torque loads with high recurring overload (e.g. refiners, extruders, rock crushers) MUST be sized on the
heavy-duty continuous current at the actual supply voltage, not the normal-duty current or the kW label. Normal-duty is for
variable-torque/light-overload loads (fans, pumps at BEP).
Method:
1. Read the motor nameplate full-load current (FLC) at its rated voltage.
2. Correct FLC to the measured supply voltage: a lower supply voltage raises the current for the same shaft power (I ∝ 1/V for
a given P, cos φ, η). For example, a 42 A / 400 V motor draws ≈ 44 A at a 380 V supply.
3. Identify the load's duty class from the driven-machine data sheet or process duty profile. Constant-torque loads with
recurring overload are heavy-duty.
4. Select the smallest frame whose heavy-duty continuous output current meets or exceeds the corrected FLC — for
heavy-duty loads. For normal-duty loads, use the ND column.
5. Verify the fault-level compliance against §3.
Do not substitute the ND current when the load is heavy-duty. The '22 kW' frame (DTX-45) carries a 22 kW label because its
ND column matches a 22 kW / 42 A ND motor at 400 V — its heavy-duty continuous current is 38 A, which is a different rating
 for a different duty class.



3. Short-circuit rating (Icc / SCCR) — conditional
Each frame in the DTX Series has a conditional short-circuit current rating in accordance with IEC 61800-5-1 §4.3.6.4 (a).
The conditional Icc is valid only when the exact specified aR semiconductor coordinating fuse listed in §1.1 is fitted
upstream of the drive input terminals, sized and located per this datasheet. The fuse is an integral part of the SCCR — it is
not interchangeable with a gG, gM, MCB, or MCCB of equivalent nominal rating.
Where no coordinating fuse (or a non-specified device) is fitted upstream, the standalone Icc applies. The standalone rating
is the drive's own withstand without upstream current limitation.

3.2 Notes on the coordinating fuse

• Must be an aR-class semiconductor fuse to IEC 60269-4, rated ≥ 690 V AC.
• Must be located in the drive's own supply feeder, not shared with other loads.
• Must be sized exactly per §4 — a smaller fuse compromises let-through coordination, a larger fuse compromises the
semiconductor protection basis of the rating.
• The conditional rating is not extended by the presence of an additional upstream MCCB or ACB.

  Lead Electrical Engineer (technical sign-off)       Red James               Marlden Panel Products

  H&S / Compliance Manager (permit authority)         Callum Bretherton       Marlden Panel Products

  Senior Maintenance Electrician (switchgear)         Dougie Fenwick          Marlden Panel Products

  Maintenance Electrician — motors & drives           Priya Nandwani          Marlden Panel Products

  Maintenance Electrician — safety & LOTO             Marcus Odigie           Marlden Panel Products

  Controls / PLC Engineer                             Fiona Machar            Marlden Panel Products

  VFD Vendor Project Engineer (support)               Amara Petrossian        DriveTec Systems GmbH
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All persons working on or opening a VFD cubicle must be electrically competent, familiar with this method statement, and named on the current permit-to-work.

1.3 Hazard identification and risk assessment

The following hazards are identified for the scope of this method statement. All controls listed below shall be in place before work begins.

-   Hazard 1 — Electric shock from 400 V AC supply. Persons at risk: electrical workers and adjacent personnel. Controls: upstream isolation and lock-off per Section 3; use of insulated tools; PPE per Section 2. Residual risk rating: Low. Reference: LOTO procedure.

-   Hazard 2 — Stored-energy release from DC-bus capacitors. Persons at risk: any person opening a VFD cubicle. Controls: mandatory discharge wait and prove-dead at drive DC-bus terminals per Section 3 Steps 3–4; permit-to-work per permit-to-work. Residual risk rating: Low. Reference: IEC 61800-5-1 (IEC 61800-5-1 extract).

-   Hazard 3 — Arc flash from inadvertent energisation during work. Persons at risk: personnel in front of open cubicle. Controls: LOTO with personal padlocks per Section 3 Step 2; arc-rated PPE per Section 2; second-competent-person presence. Residual risk rating: Low. Reference: LOTO procedure.

-   Hazard 4 — Manual handling of cubicle panels, drives and cables. Persons at risk: any worker handling components. Controls: two-person lift for panels > 20 kg; use of mechanical aids; PPE per Section 2. Residual risk rating: Low.

-   Hazard 5 — IR-test voltage applied to drive electronics. Persons at risk: drive semiconductors (equipment); operators handling exposed conductors. Controls: physical disconnection of drive output U/V/W before applying IR test per Section 4. Residual risk rating: Low.

2. PPE and site rules

-   Arc-rated coverall or two-layer arc-rated clothing to the site electrical PPE matrix; long sleeves fastened.

-   Class 0 (1 kV) insulated gloves with leather over-protectors when handling conductors or proving-dead. Gloves visually inspected and pressure-tested within calibration.

-   Arc-rated face shield with balaclava for cubicle opening and voltage-proving at DC-bus terminals.

-   Safety footwear (ESD, S3), safety glasses under the face shield, hard hat where indicated by site notices in the MCC room.

-   Non-conductive matting at the front of any cubicle being opened.

-   No lone working on VFD cubicles. A second competent person is required within line-of-sight for every energised-adjacent task.

-   Two-way radios on Channel 2; mobile phones only on breaks (MCC room is EMI-sensitive during drive commissioning).

-   Follow the site LOTO and permit-to-work procedure (LOTO procedure) at all times.

3. Safe sequence for cubicle access — ANY VFD cubicle

This sequence applies to every access to any DriveTec DTX drive cubicle on Line 2 — commissioning access, IR testing, parameter loading, fault-finding and post-energisation intervention.

STEP 1 — Notify and prepare permit-to-work (PTW). Requesting party notifies the H&S/Compliance Manager (C. Bretherton) and the Lead Electrical Engineer (R. James). A permit-to-work (reference PTW-L2-#### — see permit-to-work PTW-L2-0087 for this cubicle) is raised for the specific cubicle. Scope, personnel, isolation points and expected duration are recorded on the PTW.

STEP 2 — Upstream isolation at incomer, apply personal lock and tag, log in isolation certificate. The nominated electrician (M. Odigie or delegate) opens the upstream incomer feeding the target cubicle, applies a personal padlock and danger tag, and completes the isolation certificate in the site isolation log. ISO number, cubicle reference, time of isolation, isolator location, padlock serial and tag serial are recorded before proceeding.

STEP 3 — WAIT the manufacturer-stated DC-bus discharge time. Wait the drive manufacturer-stated safe DC-bus discharge time before opening the cubicle. The required wait time is stated in the drive manufacturer stored-energy documentation held in the drive documentation pack. The wait begins at the moment the upstream isolation is locked off and tagged, and must be observed in full before any panel door is opened.

STEP 4 — Prove-dead at DRIVE DC-BUS TERMINALS with an approved two-pole voltage indicator. After the manufacturer-stated discharge time has elapsed, the electrician performing the work must prove-dead at drive DC-bus terminals across DC+ to DC−, DC+ to PE and DC− to PE, using the approved two-pole voltage indicator held on the calibrated test-gear register (test-gear register): Fluke T150, asset reference MP-VP-012, rated 690 V AC/DC. The indicator shall itself be verified before and after the prove-dead using the proving unit held on the same register (Fluke PRV240FS, asset reference MP-VP-008), in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. The reading must be below 50 V DC on every combination before any conductor is touched. Prove-dead is performed at the drive's own DC-bus test terminals — not at the upstream isolator, not at the incoming supply terminals.

STEP 5 — Access cubicle for work. Only when Steps 1–4 are complete may the cubicle be opened and the scheduled work begin, under the PTW conditions.

STEP 6 — On completion, close cubicle, remove tools, remove tag/lock, restore supply, sign restoration in isolation log. On completion: check no tools, offcuts or fasteners remain inside the cubicle; refit any removed guards; close and secure the door. The person who applied the padlock/tag in Step 2 removes them. Supply is restored at the upstream incomer. The restoration entry is signed and timed in the isolation log, the PTW is closed by the H&S Manager, and the commissioning checklist (commissioning checklist) is updated.

3.1 MANDATORY status of Steps 3 and 4

Steps 3 and 4 are MANDATORY on every VFD cubicle access and must be applied in accordance with the LOTO procedure and the drive manufacturer discharge data.

The DC-bus capacitors inside a DTX drive retain stored energy after the AC supply is removed. Absence of voltage at the incoming supply terminals does not indicate the state of charge on the DC-bus capacitors.

3.2 Standards and procedural references

-   IEC 61800-5-1 (IEC 61800-5-1 extract) — Adjustable-speed electrical power drive systems, safety requirements. Confirms that DC-bus capacitors retain hazardous charge after supply removal; no access until the manufacturer-stated discharge time has elapsed and the equipment has been proven dead; upstream isolation alone is insufficient.

-   LOTO / Safe Isolation Procedure — VFD Addendum (LOTO procedure) — The site LOTO addendum for VFD stored energy, which requires the manufacturer-stated discharge wait to be applied in addition to the general upstream-isolation body of the procedure.

-   Manufacturer DC-bus discharge data — included in the drive documentation pack; gives the safe-access time and capacitor / resistor data to be applied before any cubicle opening.

-   permit-to-work — Permit-to-Work, Drive Cubicle (PTW-L2-0087).

-   commissioning checklist — Commissioning Checklist — carries the "DC-bus 8-min discharge before access" gate.

4. Insulation resistance (IR) testing procedure

IR testing on Line 2 motor cables is performed at 500 V DC with the calibrated insulation tester issued from the test-gear register (test-gear register). The drive output stage must be electrically isolated from the cable under test before applying test voltage — semiconductor devices in the DTX inverter section will be damaged if 500 V DC is impressed across them.

Sequence:

1.  Apply the full Section 3 sequence (Steps 1–4) to the target cubicle. Do not proceed until prove-dead at drive DC-bus terminals is complete.

2.  Isolate drive output first: disconnect the U/V/W motor-cable cores from the drive output terminals and land them clear of any drive conductor. Both ends of the cable are open — motor end already open from installation, drive end now open.

3.  Verify continuity of the cable earth screen between gland plates per the EMC bonding requirements in DTX install manual §3.2.

4.  Perform 500 V DC IR test core-to-core and core-to-earth for a minimum of 60 s per combination. Record readings on the IR test record (IR test record); minimum acceptance ≥ 100 MΩ at 20 °C.

5.  Discharge the cable after each test using the tester's integrated discharge function; confirm below 50 V before touching cores.

6.  Reconnect motor cores to drive output terminals to the torque values specified in the drive installation manual (DTX install manual). Re-terminate EMC gland with 360° screen contact at the MCC end.

7.  Close cubicle and complete Step 6 of Section 3.

5. Commissioning procedure

Drive commissioning follows the VFD Parameter & Commissioning Guide (DTX commissioning guide) issued by DriveTec Systems GmbH. Summary sequence per drive:

8.  Confirm mechanical install, cable terminations, EMC gland bonding and earthing complete; permit and Section 3 sequence in place for parameter loading.

9.  Enter the per-motor nameplate values into the DTX parameter set from the motor's nameplate data: rated voltage, rated current, rated frequency, rated speed / pole count, cos φ, insulation class. Verify that the values entered match the physical nameplate on the motor before running.

10. Configure electronic motor thermal protection (I²t) from the nameplate rated current and service class, per DTX commissioning guide and IEC 61800-5-1 (IEC 61800-5-1 extract).

11. Run the drive's stationary auto-tune with the motor coupled but stationary; then rotating auto-tune where the driven load permits, otherwise stationary only. Log tuned stator resistance, leakage inductance and no-load current in the drive parameter record (drive parameter record).

12. Set application parameters per the refiner duty profile (refiner duty profile) — heavy-duty (150 % overload) constant-torque profile for the refiner; ramp times, current limits, skip frequencies and switching frequency (default 4 kHz).

13. Configure I/O, fieldbus mapping to the line PLC (F. Machar), fault reporting and reset behaviour.

14. First energisation: uncoupled where possible, otherwise minimum load, monitoring current, voltage, DC-bus voltage, temperature and any warnings.

15. Functional / loaded runs against the commissioning checklist (commissioning checklist). Sign off each row; countersign by R. James before hand-over.

Any parameter deviation from DTX commissioning guide or from motor nameplate register nameplate values must be raised via the project RFI process and recorded on drive parameter record before running the motor.

6. Emergency response

6.1 Electric shock or arc-flash incident

-   Do not touch the casualty until the supply is confirmed isolated. Trip the upstream incomer if not already open; if unable to isolate, use a dry insulating rescue implement.

-   Call site first-aid via extension 999 (internal) and dial 999 (external ambulance). Site address for ambulance: Marlden Works, Ashcombe Industrial Estate, Unit 4, Beattock Road, Dumfries DG1 4XR.

-   Begin CPR / defibrillation as trained; the nearest AED is mounted at the MCC-room entrance.

-   All electric shock casualties, regardless of apparent condition, are transported to hospital for cardiac observation.

-   Preserve the scene; do not re-energise. Notify R. James and C. Bretherton immediately.

6.2 Fire in the MCC / drive cubicle

-   Break glass on the nearest MCC-room fire call point. Isolate at the 11 kV/LV transformer LV incomer where safe to do so; do not open a burning cubicle.

-   Use CO₂ extinguishers only on electrical fires; water and foam are prohibited on live electrical equipment.

-   Evacuate to the Line 2 assembly point (north-east gate). Roll-call by Plant Manager (G. Sutcliffe) or deputy.

6.3 Injury from stored energy / capacitor discharge

Treat as electric shock (6.1). Additionally record the incident on the isolation log against the ISO entry for the cubicle involved, and quarantine the cubicle pending investigation by R. James, C. Bretherton and DriveTec vendor support (A. Petrossian).

6.4 Reporting and stop-work authority

Any person on site has stop-work authority for a suspected unsafe condition on a VFD cubicle — in particular, any doubt over whether the Section 3 sequence has been completed. Stop-work is exercised without penalty and is escalated to R. James and C. Bretherton. Work does not resume until the Section 3 sequence has been re-verified and the PTW re-endorsed.

End of Method Statement MS-L2VFD-01, Rev B.

Marlden Panel Products — Standards Library — Extract from IEC 61800-3:
Adjustable Speed Electrical Power Drive Systems — Part 3: EMC
requirements — Version 2024-05
Reference: IEC 61800-3 (Adjustable Speed Electrical Power Drive Systems — Part 3)
Subject: EMC / motor cabling — screening and screen termination for VFD-fed motor circuits
Document ID: MPP-STD-EXT-IEC61800-3 · Version 2024-05
Prepared by: Marlden Panel Products — Standards Library
Applies to: All power drive system (PDS) motor circuits on the Marlden site



1. Principle
A VFD-fed motor cable is not an ordinary power cable. The pulse-width-modulated (PWM) output of the drive impresses
steep-edged voltage transitions on the motor terminals, and each transition drives a significant high-frequency
common-mode current back through the cable and the surrounding earth-return system. IEC 61800-3 treats this
common-mode current as the dominant EMC path of the drive/motor combination — it is the mechanism behind conducted
and radiated emissions in the MHz range, and it is the mechanism behind common-mode-driven bearing currents in the
motor.
The return path for this high-frequency common-mode current must be a low-impedance screen bonded correctly at both
ends of the cable. Any interruption, high-impedance connection or single-point termination diverts the return current into
unintended paths (structural steel, adjacent cable armouring, instrumentation earths, motor bearings), producing the
emissions and bearing-current phenomena the standard is written to prevent.

2. Cable construction
VFD motor cables shall be SCREENED and preferably SYMMETRICAL (three symmetric power cores + three
symmetric earth cores + concentric copper screen) rated for the PWM output.
The symmetrical construction (three power cores of equal geometry with three interleaved protective-earth conductors,
enclosed by a concentric copper braid or copper-tape screen) minimises the common-mode inductance seen by the drive
output and gives a defined low-impedance path for the return current at high frequency. The cable insulation and screen
system shall be rated for the peak terminal voltages and dV/dt characteristic of PWM inverter output (typically up to ~2×
DC-bus voltage with cable reflection).
Unscreened cable is not acceptable for VFD motor circuits. Unscreened multi-core power cable — of the type used
historically on direct-on-line and soft-starter feeders — provides no defined return path for common-mode current and does
not satisfy Part 3 of the standard for a power drive system output.

3. Screen termination
The screen shall be terminated with a low-impedance 360° connection at BOTH ENDS of the cable (drive/MCC end
and motor terminal-box end), typically via an EMC cable gland with continuous screen-to-plate contact.
The termination requirements are:
• Drive/MCC end: the cable screen is landed on the gland plate of the drive cubicle (or on a dedicated earthing bar bonded to
the cubicle back-plate) through an EMC cable gland that makes continuous 360° contact between the exposed screen and
the metallic gland body.
• Motor terminal-box end: the cable screen is landed on the motor terminal-box gland plate through an equivalent EMC
cable gland, again making continuous 360° screen-to-body contact.
• Both glands shall bond to metalwork that is itself part of the protective-earth system, so that the screen-to-earth path at each
end is of the lowest achievable impedance at the switching-frequency harmonics of the drive output.
• The exposed screen length inside the gland shall be the full circumference of the cable; pigtail or "flag" terminations of the
screen shall not be used at either end of a VFD motor cable, as they introduce a series inductance that defeats the purpose of
the screen at HF.

4. Distinction from instrumentation practice
Single-end earthing (pigtail) is the correct convention for INSTRUMENTATION SIGNAL SCREENS to avoid
low-frequency earth loops. It is the WRONG practice for VFD power motor cables because it leaves high-frequency
common-mode current with no low-impedance return path — worsening EMC emissions and increasing
bearing-current stress.
The two conventions address different physics and must not be confused on site:

 Aspect                                     Instrumentation signal screen               VFD power motor cable screen
  Objective                                 Reject low-frequency (50/60 Hz)           Provide a low-impedance
                                           magnetic pickup and prevent               high-frequency return path for
                                           circulating currents in a                 common-mode current driven by PWM
                                           common-mode loop between two              switching (kHz–MHz range)
                                           earthed instrument enclosures
 Correct termination                       Single-end earth (typically at the        360° screen-to-metal termination at
                                           control-panel/receiver end); pigtail      both ends via EMC cable gland
                                           acceptable
 Failure mode of wrong bonding             Circulating 50 Hz loop current if         Radiated/conducted EMC emissions
                                           bonded at both ends                       and bearing-current damage if bonded
                                                                                     single-end

The screen-termination requirement for VFD power motor cables is a low-impedance 360° connection at both ends of the
cable — this is the requirement specified by IEC 61800-3 for the high-frequency return path.

5. Consequences of incorrect bonding
Where the screen of a VFD motor cable is left unterminated, terminated by pigtail, or bonded at only one end, the following
consequences shall be expected:
• Increased radiated and conducted EMC emissions. Common-mode current returns through unintended paths (steelwork,
cable tray, armour of adjacent cables), radiating at the switching-frequency harmonics and their sidebands. The installation
may fail the emission limits of IEC 61800-3 for its declared environment category (C1/C2/C3).
• Bearing-current damage in the motor. With no low-impedance HF return at the motor end, common-mode current returns
through the motor shaft and bearings, producing electric-discharge machining (EDM) pitting, fluting and premature bearing
failure — most severe in motors without inverter-duty insulated bearings or shaft-grounding devices.
• Malfunction of adjacent instrumentation. HF common-mode current radiated or coupled from an incorrectly bonded VFD
motor cable is a common cause of intermittent faults on 4–20 mA loops, thermocouple inputs, encoder feedback and fieldbus
segments routed near the drive-to-motor run.

Cross-references (Marlden Standards Library):
• Drive install manual (screened/symmetrical VFD cable specification)
• EMC cable gland datasheet — KCC-EMC Series (Kelbrook Cable Components Ltd)
• IEC 60034-18-41 extract — inverter-duty motor insulation
• Bearing-current application note (DriveTec Systems GmbH)
End of extract — Page 1 of 1

Marlden Panel Products — Standards Library
Extract from IEC 60364-5-52: Wiring Systems — Current-carrying capacity
Prepared by: Engineering Standards Library
Version 2024-03
Document ref: MPP-STD-SUM-05



1. Principle
A cable's tabulated current-carrying capacity is a base value quoted for a defined reference installation and reference ambient
temperature. Before that tabulated value can be compared with the circuit's design current Ib, it must be corrected by every
applicable installation factor.
The corrected (in-service) capacity of the conductor is:
Iz = It × (product of applicable correction factors)
Equivalently, the minimum tabulated capacity that the selected conductor must satisfy is:
It ≥ Ib / (product of applicable correction factors)
Selecting a conductor against the raw tabulated rating — i.e. without applying the correction factors that the installation calls
for — will under-size the cable. This applies whether one factor or several are in force.

2. Grouping factor *Cg*
For circuits bunched in adjacent enclosures/cubicles (e.g. drive cubicles in the same MCC section), apply grouping factor Cg
= 0.80 (four to six circuits, touching, in air).
This reflects that neighbouring loaded conductors mutually raise each other's operating temperature; the tabulated
single-circuit rating over-states the capacity actually available to any one of the bunched circuits.

3. Ambient-temperature factor *Ca*
For elevated ambient (MCC room measured ~45 °C vs 30 °C tabulated base), 90 °C XLPE conductor, IEC 60364-5-52 Annex
B gives Ca = 0.87.
The tabulated ratings in the current-carrying-capacity tables assume 30 °C ambient for cables in air. Where the room where
the cable runs is measurably hotter, the conductor has less headroom above ambient before reaching its permitted operating
temperature, and its usable capacity falls accordingly.

4. Application — factors combine
Cg and Ca apply in combination. Where both conditions are present (bunched circuits and elevated ambient), the correction
factors multiply:
required tabulated capacity = Ib / (Cg × Ca)
Applying only one factor when both apply is an under-application of the derating rule and will result in a conductor sized below
the standard's requirement.

5. Tabulated ratings (IEC 60364-5-52)
4-core XLPE/SWA cable installed in air (Reference method E), 30 °C ambient, single circuit:

 Conductor size                                                   Tabulated current-carrying capacity
 4 mm²                                                            38 A
 6 mm² = 49 A                                                     49 A
 10 mm² = 66 A                                                    66 A
 16 mm²                                                           87 A
 25 mm²                                                           114 A

These are the base tabulated values It. They must be reduced by the applicable Cg and Ca factors before being compared
with the circuit design current.

6. Annex E — triplen-harmonic derating
 The triplen-harmonic derating in Annex E applies only where 3rd/9th-order harmonic content is significant (e.g. balanced
non-linear single-phase loads on shared neutrals). Because triplen harmonics on the three phases are in-phase and therefore
sum — rather than cancel — in a shared neutral, they cause additional neutral loading and heating that the Annex E factor
accounts for.
It does not apply to 6-pulse drive input feeders whose spectrum is dominated by 5th/7th/11th/13th (non-triplen). A 6-pulse
rectifier's characteristic harmonics are of order 6k ± 1 (5, 7, 11, 13, …); the 3rd is negligible. Reaching for Annex E in that
situation over-derates the cable and misapplies the standard.

7. Worked example (generic)
For a 30 A circuit with Cg = 0.80 and Ca = 0.87:
• required tabulated capacity = *Ib* / (*Cg* × *Ca*) = 30 / (0.80 × 0.87) = 43.1 A
• select a conductor whose tabulated rating in the applicable installation method meets or exceeds 43.1 A.

Marlden Standards Summary — IEC 60364-5-52 (MPP-STD-SUM-05) — Version 2024-03 — Page 1

Site Supply / Power-Quality Survey — Marlden Works, Dumfries

Prepared: Engineering, Marlden Panel Products Ltd

Document ref: MPP-L2-PQ-01

Survey date: 06/15/2026

Instrument: Fluke 435-II Power Quality Analyzer (Cal cert MP-PQ-012, cal exp 01/2027)

Survey point: Line 2 MCC incoming busbar (Section A busbar tee-off, downstream of the site 400 V main LV switchboard)

Survey duration: 7 days continuous (06/08/2026 00:00 to 06/15/2026 00:00), 10-minute aggregation per IEC 61000-4-30

1. Site Incoming Supply Arrangement

The Marlden Works site is fed from the Scottish Power 11 kV distribution network via a dedicated site incomer feeding the on-site substation. The single-line arrangement from utility incomer to the Line 2 MCC busbar is as follows:

-   HV incomer: 11 kV, 3-phase, Scottish Power distribution feed, terminating at the site ring-main unit in the substation.

-   Site distribution transformer: Dry-type, 1000 kVA, 11 kV / 400 V, vector group Dyn11, impedance %Z = 6%. Installed 2018, primary fuse-switch on the HV side, LV neutral solidly earthed at the transformer star point (site earthing terminal).

-   LV distribution: Cable run from the transformer LV terminals to the site main LV switchboard, and from there via a dedicated 4-core armoured feeder to the Line 2 MCC incomer.

-   LV system: 400 V nominal, 3-phase 4-wire, 50 Hz, TN-S earthing arrangement — separate protective conductor bonded to the site earth bar at the transformer neutral point; no combined PEN downstream of the transformer.

The survey instrument was clamped at the Line 2 MCC busbar, phase-to-phase and phase-to-neutral, over the full 7-day window. The MCC was in its shutdown state during the survey (Line 2 loads not running) so the recorded values represent the background site condition presented to the new drives when they are energised.

2. Voltage Measurements at the Line 2 MCC Busbar

Aggregated values across the 7-day window at the Line 2 MCC incoming busbar:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Quantity                                                    Measured value           Notes
  ----------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------
  Nominal supply voltage                                      400 V (phase-to-phase)   System nominal

  Mean LV voltage (7-day)                                     380 V (phase-to-phase)   Approximately 5% below nominal

  Voltage stability (95th percentile band)                    ±2% about the mean       Well inside EN 50160 ±10% envelope

  Minimum recorded (10-min avg)                               376 V                    06/11/2026 14:20, coincident with Line 3 laminator loading

  Maximum recorded (10-min avg)                               385 V                    06/13/2026 03:10, off-shift period

  Frequency                                                   50.0 Hz (±0.05 Hz)       Nominal

  Voltage unbalance (negative-sequence / positive-sequence)   0.8%                     Within EN 50160 2% limit
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The mean supply voltage sits consistently below the 400 V nominal across the survey window. This is the site's steady-state condition and is not attributable to a transient event; the Scottish Power feed at this end of the Ashcombe Estate spur has historically run on the low side of nominal. The narrow ±2% stability band indicates a stiff supply with no significant voltage flicker or sag events during the survey.

3. Motor-Side Implication for the Line 2 Refiner Drive

For a given mechanical shaft power at the motor, a reduced terminal voltage causes a proportional rise in stator current. The Line 2 refiner motor (Bramwell BEM-180L-4A, 22 kW, IEC 180L frame) carries a nameplate full-load current of 42 A at the nameplate voltage of 400 V. Adjusting to the measured supply:

Motor nameplate FLC 42 A at 400 V rises to approximately 44 A at the measured supply of 380 V for the same shaft power (same kW).

Use 44 A / 380 V as the motor-side input to drive sizing. The drive output current rating (heavy-duty column for the refiner duty class per the duty profile) must be selected against this 44 A figure, not against the 42 A nameplate value at nominal 400 V.

This adjustment applies at the motor terminals and reflects the current the drive must deliver on its output stage to maintain the required shaft power at the site's actual supply condition. It is independent of the drive input current, which is set by the drive's own topology (6-pulse rectifier front end) and DC-bus behaviour, and is not corrected here.

4. Background Harmonic Content

Voltage-side harmonic distortion measured at the Line 2 MCC busbar, background condition (Line 2 loads off):

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Quantity                                                    Measured value                                            Reference
  ----------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Voltage THD (Uh, phase-to-neutral, 7-day 95th percentile)   ~3.5%                                                     Compatibility level per IEC 61000-2-2 for public LV supply systems

  Dominant harmonic orders                                    5th (2.4%), 7th (1.6%), 11th (0.7%)                       Non-triplen, characteristic of upstream 6-pulse rectifier population on the estate spur

  Triplen content (3rd, 9th)                                  <0.4% each                                                Low; no significant single-phase non-linear contribution

  Voltage THD limit reference                                 8% (IEEE 519 / IEC 61000-2-4 Class 2, industrial plant)   Measured value well inside limit
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The measured 3.5% background THD is within the IEEE 519 and IEC 61000-2-2 compatibility-level envelopes for this class of connection. The spectrum is characteristically non-triplen (5th/7th/11th/13th dominant), consistent with 6-pulse converter loads elsewhere on the estate spur and with the transformer Dyn11 vector group (which blocks triplen harmonics from passing to the HV network).

The new Line 2 VFDs will contribute additional 6-pulse input harmonics to the busbar when energised; the incremental harmonic impact is addressed in the separate Line 2 harmonic assessment and is not re-evaluated here.

5. Interaction with Cable-Sizing Records

The Line 2 cable schedule records the refiner drive feeder at a design current (Ib) of 45 A. The feeder design current on the schedule is not further voltage-corrected in this survey record — the 42 A → 44 A adjustment above is a motor-side sizing figure for selecting the drive output frame, and is distinct from the feeder-side design current Ib used for cable-sizing derating per IEC 60364-5-52.

The two figures serve different purposes and must not be conflated:

-   44 A at 380 V — motor terminal current; input to drive output-frame selection (heavy-duty rating check).

-   45 A — feeder design current on the cable schedule; input to conductor cross-section calculation.

6. Survey Instrument and Traceability

-   Instrument: Fluke 435-II Series II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer, s/n 33471024

-   Calibration certificate: MP-PQ-012 (Marlden test-gear register)

-   Calibration expiry: 01/2027 — valid at time of survey

-   Class A per IEC 61000-4-30 for voltage, frequency, unbalance and harmonics

-   Voltage inputs: direct connection at MCC incomer test points, phase-to-phase and phase-to-neutral

-   Current inputs: Fluke i430flex-TF flexible current probes on incomer cables (used for reference / load profile only; MCC was off-load for the survey window)

-   Aggregation: 10-minute intervals, 7-day continuous recording

7. Summary

The Line 2 MCC busbar sees a stiff, low-distortion supply that sits consistently below the 400 V nominal at a mean of 380 V. Voltage stability, frequency, unbalance and background THD are all within EN 50160 / IEC 61000-2-2 / IEEE 519 envelopes. The one measurement that carries directly into the VFD upgrade design is the sub-nominal steady-state voltage, which raises the refiner motor's required current from the 42 A nameplate value to approximately 44 A at the actual supply — the figure to be used when selecting the refiner drive's output rating.

End of record.
